definition.question: does a joint hit over all keys of one sentence fix the record choice?
definition.selection_rule: candidate = every corpus record that contains ALL literal byte spans the R15 read matched in the question; exactly one candidate -> emit it; zero -> no_match, no bytes; two or more -> ambiguous_multiple_records, no bytes
definition.deleted_fallback: the lowest-address path (SPEC 16.2 address_order) is deleted from selection; it is not reachable by any flag, and no default address is returned

groups.primary: the 20 describe sentences (4 objects x 5 places x 1 variant); 40 entity slots
groups.names: 20 authored name-worded questions 让{object}到{place}。 (secondary, not judged)
groups.aliases: 9 authored aliases alone, one per entity (secondary, not judged)

definition.unit: frozen SPEC 16.2 unit: a complete record or a complete sentence; no third unit
definition.L1: fabricated 0, illegal 0, UTF-8 decodable 100%, boundary legal 100%
definition.L2: emitted bytes equal record[start:end] byte for byte; must be 1.0
definition.L3: four classes per entity slot: answered_correct / pointed_wrong / abstained / should_answer_missing; ambiguous_multiple_records counts as abstained and no_match as should_answer_missing, each also reported by name
definition.paired_numbers: pairing_matches and answers_lost are reported side by side; answers_lost = 40 minus the slots that emitted bytes, i.e. what was paid to remove wrong pairings
definition.closed_state: the nine closed-state readings stay equal before and after
definition.training: zero training, zero optimizer steps, zero Adam, zero confirm
definition.diagnostics: two extra groups were added AFTER the first pass, when the name group turned out to have no keys at all: paraphrase = the 60 name-worded records, mixed = 9 alias + description questions.  They are reported for the cost column only and never enter the verdict

primary.why: a describe sentence's two key spans only co-occur in that pair's describe record, so the joint hit is a singleton and the record is the asked one

names.why: names appear in the needs / hope / state records of the same pair: three records

aliases.why: the alias wording is not in the corpus at all

paraphrase.why: needs / hope / state sentences are name-worded and names are not keys

mixed.why: one key is an alias (absent from the corpus), so a joint hit cannot exist

criteria.structural: signature, literal, AST and behaviour checks all report the fallback unreachable; any one failing blocks the verdict
criteria.l1: fabricated 0, illegal 0, utf8 all, boundary all
criteria.loss: pairing_matches and answers_lost both reported, never only the first
criteria.samples: at least 3 real outputs, including one wrong->correct and one wrong->uncertain
